solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Visitors have no time to meet Doctor, so must debate his identity

indicators.note: the visitors lack something, so a letter is removed from their word

parts.note: visitors to a house are guests
Doctor Who is the time-travelling hero of the long-running BBC television series

explanation.surface: Guests arrive and must argue over the identity of the doctor they have come to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have no' takes one T out of GUESTS to leave GUESS. 'Doctor' as a solo word is WHO, from the BBC series.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what you say when inviting someone to puzzle out a person's identity, matching the debate over who he is.

clue.text: Tasteless fish is supremely horrid!

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: supremely means at the very top, so only the leading letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a tasteless fish dish is utterly horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the top of 'horrid' is its first letter, H.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something showy and vulgar, lacking refinement in style.

clue.text: Meaning to force result

definitions.meaning: the import or sense of words
an outcome or consequence produced by a cause

explanation.walkthrough: Three short definitions sit side by side, with 'to' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers sense or gist, legal operation, and a consequence, three distinct dictionary meanings.

clue.text: Old Eastern Railways diverted northwards

indicators.note: in a down clue going northwards means reading from the bottom up, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: railway routes are lines

explanation.surface: Ancient Eastern railway lines have been rerouted towards the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted northwards' reverses E plus LINES, ELINES, as the light is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble with age, so describing someone elderly and in decline, a sense of old age.

clue.text: "Mrs" Doris Heron sadly doesn't get out much

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: A housewife called Doris Heron rarely leaves the house, which is rather sad.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang, popularised by the TV comedy Minder, for one's wife; the clue's 'doesn't get out much' adds to the picture of a stay-at-home spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocular British slang for a man's wife, the woman who rules the home, hence Mrs.

clue.text: Fantastic guide to PC

definitions.meaning: British informal praise meaning excellent or marvellous
a step-by-step software assistant that leads a computer user through setting something up

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both old British slang for excellent and the name for an installation helper on a computer.

clue.text: Decision made, having worshipped

indicators.note: made here means fashioned or reconstructed, so the letters are reworked into a new word

explanation.surface: A decision has been reached after a period of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is the anagram signal, reshaping the letters of 'Decision'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be turned into an icon is to be idolised or revered, so something treated with worship.

clue.text: Certain instrument on which sailors introduce Offenbach

parts.note: ABs, able seamen, are the crossword's standard sailors

indicators.note: the start of a name is what introduces it, so only the leading letter is taken

parts.note: the lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Sailors perform Offenbach on a particular musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on which' means the sailors and the composer's initial sit above the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute and certain are synonyms, both meaning definite and beyond doubt.

clue.text: Conservative benefactor initially reported to receiver

indicators.note: initially says the spoken piece comes first, before the party member
reported means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a donor is a benefactor who gives money
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory donor was first reported to the official receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the benefactor's word loses its final R when spoken; 'initially' puts that sound before the party member.
explanation.definitionFit: A donatory is the recipient of a gift or donation, so one who receives.

clue.text: Plant soldier's decorations

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers in crosswords
finery is showy decoration or fine clothing

explanation.surface: A gardener admires a soldier's ornamental greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' is industrial, a factory for purifying oil or sugar, not something growing.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial works is called a plant, and a refinery is such a works.

clue.text: Convenience of having guard partially relax

parts.note: a public convenience is a lavatory, a loo

indicators.note: only part of the guard's word is used, the tail end dropped

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard

explanation.surface: A toilet with an attendant lets one ease up a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' trims SENTRY to SEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken a grip or make less tight is to ease or relax it.

clue.text: In the wild, gnu licks its young

indicators.note: in the wild suggests something untamed and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Out on the savannah a wildebeest licks its calf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the wild' scrambles the letters of 'gnu licks'.
explanation.definitionFit: A young animal still feeding on its mother's milk is called a suckling.

clue.text: Told to send account for accommodation

indicators.note: told means spoken aloud, so the phrase is taken by sound

parts.note: sending an account to someone is to bill it

explanation.surface: Someone was instructed to dispatch an invoice for lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill it' said quickly sounds like BILLET, a soldier's lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is lodging, especially quarters for soldiers in a private house.

clue.text: Best performance put down to the occasion

parts.note: to put something down on paper is to record it
an occasion is a time, as in 'on that occasion'

explanation.surface: An outstanding achievement was written up for the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A record time is the fastest ever achieved, the top result in a race.

clue.text: Passion for landlord expressed in words

parts.note: passion is strong love
one who lets property is a letter

explanation.surface: A tenant writes of their passion for the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landlord' gives LETTER, one who lets, not the written kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic note puts feelings into writing, passion set out on paper.

clue.text: Underhand attempt to drink special latte

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a shy is a try or throw, as in having a shy at something

indicators.note: special suggests something made differently, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone sneakily tries to drink a special coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges the coffee, and 'to drink' puts that inside the attempt word, between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean secretive and furtive, done so as to avoid notice.

clue.text: Present distribution agents

parts.note: the creatures that pull Santa's sleigh as he delivers gifts at Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: Santa's antlered team pull the sleigh that delivers Christmas gifts, so they are the deliverers of presents.

clue.text: Is it right to con such people?

parts.note: well can mean right or proper, as in 'it is well that'
taken as written
to do someone is to swindle or con them

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether it is fair to swindle the rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such people' points back to the rich as the natural targets of a con; the phrase as a noun means the wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The affluent are the comfortably off, the sort of people a swindler would pick.

clue.text: Time was when we all got started

definitions.text: Time was when we all got started

parts.words: Time was when we all got started
parts.note: the very beginning of time, a date that predates everyone

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a very long time ago, the earliest imaginable date, when everything began.

clue.text: Opening pairs slither along ominous course

indicators.note: opening pairs means the first two letters of each following word

explanation.surface: A skier slithers along a menacing downhill track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening pairs' takes two letters from each word: SL, AL, OM.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a zigzag ski course between poles or gates.

clue.text: She left poor shivering maiden

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letters of the first word are taken away
poor suggests a bad state, so the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman abandoned a wretched, trembling young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S, H, E out of SHIVERING and 'poor' rearranges the leftovers IVRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A virgin is a maiden, a young unmarried woman in old usage.

clue.text: Backtracking, adviser tempers certain measures

indicators.note: Backtracking says the hidden letters are read backwards
certain means some of, so only a run of letters from the preceding words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Having changed course, a consultant moderates some policies.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'certain measures' as the definition, leaving the hidden step with no signal; 'certain' (some of) is that signal, and 'Backtracking' turns SERTEM round.
explanation.definitionFit: A metre is a unit of length, so these are specific units of measurement.

clue.text: History of girl clearing out of Leeds

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

indicators.note: clearing out empties the inside of the city's name, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A tale of a young woman leaving Leeds, a city in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds emptied out leaves L and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are yearly records, a written chronicle of events.

clue.text: Songstress gets assistance in Australian city

indicators.note: in places the help inside the singer's name

parts.note: Adele is the British singer
aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: A singer is helped while touring a city in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Adele is the British singer-songwriter; 'in' places the help inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia.

clue.text: Enough heartfelt remorse to make one shake

indicators.note: enough means just a sufficient part, so only some of the following letters are taken

explanation.surface: Sincere regret is enough to make anyone tremble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enough' signals that only a stretch of 'heartfelt remorse' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a shaking or quivering, so a shake.

clue.text: Grave ill afflicted country dweller

indicators.note: afflicted suggests something troubled and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rural resident is seriously ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afflicted' rearranges 'Grave ill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A villager lives in a village, in the countryside.

clue.text: Plant needed to put new facade on school

indicators.note: a facade is the front, so the first letter is replaced

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school in north-west London

explanation.surface: A plant is needed to give a school building a new front.
explanation.walkthrough: The new front letter is Y in place of H.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a flowering herb with feathery leaves, also called milfoil.

clue.text: Terrible misfortune of missing the station

indicators.note: terrible suggests havoc, so the letters are thrown into a new order
missing means the short word's letters are absent from the pool

explanation.surface: A dreadful accident happened, missing the station.
explanation.walkthrough: MISFORTUNE without O and F leaves MISRTUNE, which 'Terrible' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the end station on a railway or bus line.
